title: Humility
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Humility is lowliness before God that rejects pride, self-exaltation, and self-reliance. The humble person receives grace, serves others, and recognizes dependence on the Lord.
summary: Humility is lowliness before God that rejects pride, self-exaltation, and self-reliance. The humble person receives grace, serves others, and recognizes dependence on the Lord.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the supreme example of humility. Though He is Lord, He humbled Himself, served, obeyed the Father, and went to the cross for sinners.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Humility begins with seeing God rightly. Pride grows when people forget their dependence, guilt, weakness, and need for grace. Humility bows before God as Creator, Judge, Savior, and Lord.

Jesus shows humility without weakness or falsehood. He did not deny His identity, but He took the form of a servant. Christian humility is not self-hatred; it is truthful lowliness before God and others.

Humility receives correction, serves quietly, refuses superiority, and depends on grace. God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Pride can hide inside religious knowledge, ministry service, moral improvement, or comparison with others. It is dangerous because it resists grace while pretending to be strong.

This doctrine calls believers into the way of Christ. The Lord of glory humbled Himself; His followers cannot make pride their way of life.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Humble yourself before God. Confess pride, stop comparing yourself to others, receive correction, serve without needing attention, and remember that every good thing you have is grace. Look to Christ, who humbled Himself to save you.
